stem: How are most dietary lipids usually transported after absorption?

options.text: They usually enter the portal venous system directly as chylomicrons
They are usually absorbed through the lymphatic system as chylomicrons
They are usually transported in bile through the portal system
They are excreted by the kidneys before intestinal absorption
They are carried in erythrocytes to the liver

explanation: Most dietary lipids are absorbed through the lymphatic system as chylomicrons. This is the usual post-absorptive transport pathway, with only some shorter-chain fats entering the portal venous system more directly.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Diarrhoea and Malabsorption

rationale: Most absorbed lipids travel via the lymphatic system as chylomicrons.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because most dietary lipids do not enter the portal venous system directly as chylomicrons; that is not the usual pathway.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because most dietary lipids are packaged as chylomicrons and absorbed into the lymphatic system before reaching the bloodstream.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because bile salts aid fat solubilisation and digestion, but they are not the main transport form of absorbed lipids.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because lipid absorption occurs in the intestine, not by renal excretion before absorption.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because erythrocytes do not carry absorbed dietary lipids to the liver.
